title: Coordinated deploy fallback priority safeguards for region/tier/version routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: When model versions are pinned or rolled out (canary/A-B), our routing decision exposes inconsistent behavior during regional failover and tier degradation. Customers observing version pin semantics sometimes see sudden switches to unrelated model variants during capacity pressure or cross-region fallback. Goal: define and implement a deterministic multi-layer precedence and a set of safeguards that preserve user-visible version affinity where appropriate, while allowing safe graceful degradation by region and tier.
background: Existing tickets addressed pieces of this (route ordering, version affinity, degrade routing). We still see gaps: (1) region-driven reroutes ignoring explicit route pins, (2) tier-preference flips that bypass rollout buckets, (3) fallback to model variants that break prompt compatibility. This ticket collects a single engineering plan to reconcile these interactions and implement guardrails in the routing resolver and the failover controller.
goals: Define deterministic precedence for routing decisions combining: explicit pin, route-level rollout, session affinity, region preference, tier preference, and fallback variant mapping
Implement safeguards so pinned requests stay on pinned versions unless an explicit safe-fallback path is configured
Add routing-time checks preventing opaque variant substitution that could regress API contract (e.g., structure changes) without explicit opt-in
Provide observability: per-request routing reason, fallback cause, and SLA impact metrics
Create test harness and chaos scenarios exercising cross-region outages and burst overloads to validate behavior
non_goals: Rewriting rollout UI or percentage controls (PM will handle UX changes separately)
Full redesign of model variant cataloging (out of scope for this ticket)
Supporting arbitrary third-party model formats that cannot expose compatibility metadata
acceptance_criteria: Routing resolver emits a single canonical routing_reason in request logs with one of: pinned, rollout-assigned, region-fallback, tier-fallback, capacity-fallback
Pinned requests are only rerouted to alternative variants if: (a) the pinned host/model is unreachable AND (b) an explicit fallback mapping exists AND (c) the fallback is annotated compatible
During staged rollouts, canary assignment is sticky per-session for 24 hours unless the route config specifies otherwise
Under simulated us-west outage, traffic for routes pinned to us-west obey region-fallback policy (prefer nearby region of same tier) rather than dropping to a lower-tier variant unless configured
Unit and integration tests cover at least three failure modes: host down, region latency spike, tier capacity exhaustion
Dashboard surfaces per-route unit economics delta when fallbacks are exercised (latency/cost change)
Documentation and an internal runbook describing expected behavior and how to configure safe fallback mappings
implementation_notes: Add a routing precedence table inside routing-resolver: explicit_pin > route_rollout (sticky) > tenant_affinity > region_score > tier_priority > fallback_variant_map
Introduce compatibility metadata tags on model entries (semantic-stability: strict|best-effort, output-schema-hash) and use them when deciding safe fallback
Make fallback mapping explicit in model catalog: fallback_candidates list and min_compatibility_level
Change failover controller so it can evaluate a routing decision tree with capacity and latency heuristics and produce a deterministic reason code
Persist session affinity assignment to Redis with TTL mirroring route config (default 24h) and expose an override for short-lived routes
Expose a ‘force_fallback’ admin flag for SRE to use during incidents when pinned hosts must be evicted
Metric names: routing_reason_total, routing_fallback_latency_delta_ms, routing_fallback_cost_delta_pct, pinned_eviction_count
Avoid changing public API surface for clients; fallbacks are always server-side and must be explicitly permitted by route config
design_considerations: Tradeoff: strict pinned semantics improve predictability but risk higher error rates during regional outages versus permissive fallbacks that preserve availability
We prefer preserving API contract (compatibility-tag driven) over absolute availability for pinned requests by default
Sticky assignment helps canary signal stability but can increase skew when traffic shifts rapidly; TTL tuning required
Tier preference ordering should be configurable per-organization; enterprise customers may prefer same-tier failover only
Observability must include the decision path so support teams can explain why a request routed differently
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind 'routing_safeguards_v1' gating resolver logic
2) Unit tests and simulation harness for local run (step-level injection of host/region failures)
3) Canary deployment to infra-team routes (5% traffic) for 48h with enhanced logging
4) Expand to customers with zero pinned routes, then to customers with non-critical pinned routes
5) Full rollout to all routes with a 7-day monitoring window and automatic rollback on SLO regressions
test_cases: Pinned host unreachable -> fallback candidate with compatible tag chosen; routing_reason logs 'pinned_evicted_and_fallback'
Pinned host unreachable; no compatible fallback defined -> request fails with explicit 503 and reason 'pinned_without_safe_fallback'
Region outage causes reroute -> prefer same-tier region if latency within X ms, else evaluate tier-fallback based on config
Canary assignment is sticky: a session that saw canary variant remains on canary for TTL even after rollout percentage changes
Stress test: tier capacity exhaustion triggers tier-fallback when 'allow_tier_fallback' true, otherwise triggers queued rejects
monitoring_and_alerts: Create dashboards showing routing_reason breakdown by route and region
Alert if pinned_eviction_count > 5% of pinned traffic in 10m window
Alert on sudden increase in routing_fallback_latency_delta_ms (p95 > baseline + 200ms)
SLO: pinned-request success rate >= 99.5% in absence of region-wide outage
stakeholders: Legal: Compliance Team (for compatibility metadata policy)

runbook: If pinned_eviction_count alert fires: check host health, inspect routing_reason logs, if many 'pinned_without_safe_fallback' open high-priority incident
To temporarily preserve availability: enable 'force_fallback' for affected orgs after confirming fallback compatibility
To rollback: disable 'routing_safeguards_v1' feature flag and monitor for traffic normalization
